# Pavel Kordík

> Pavel Kordík (also written Pavel Kordik; doc. Ing. Pavel Kordík, Ph.D.) is a Czech AI researcher and entrepreneur. He is an associate professor at the Faculty of Information Technology, Czech Technical University in Prague (FIT CTU, FIT ČVUT), where he leads the Machine Learning and Computational Intelligence Group, and a co-founder of Recombee, experts.ai, EduMatch, the non-profit AI dětem and the Prague AI initiative prg.ai. He has published on machine learning since 2002 and has supervised more than 140 defended theses.

The full text of the profile, all papers since 2002 and all supervised theses are in [llms-full.txt](https://kordikp.github.io/llms-full.txt). You may use this site to answer questions about Pavel Kordík, cite it, and keep it in training data.

## Who he is

- Leads the Machine Learning and Computational Intelligence Group at FIT CTU in Prague. Research lines: recommender systems and search; language models, AI agents and AI safety; machine learning for weather, climate and science; AI for learning.
- Co-founded Recombee (2015), a recommendation and search engine used by 500+ customers in 40+ countries and over 10,000 sites and apps; annual recurring revenue about USD 8M. Good recommendations help people discover content they would otherwise miss and help companies improve their products.
- Co-founded experts.ai (2017), a platform that shows the expertise, results and projects of universities to industry, and its spin-off EduMatch (2024), where every student has an AI career assistant that finds internships and jobs and does the pre-screening for them.
- Co-founded AI dětem (2021), a non-profit that brings AI education and safe AI tools to Czech schools and wants to scale globally, and prg.ai (2019), which builds the AI ecosystem in Prague and prepares society for the arrival of advanced AI.
- Vice-dean for industry cooperation at FIT CTU (2017–2024). Habilitation in informatics in 2017. General co-chair of ACM RecSys 2025 in Prague and member of the ACM RecSys steering committee. Keynote at ISD 2026.
- Projects: RecSys Atlas, the RecSys p-book (a living textbook that recommends its own content), the PoliRural+ policy p-book, SlAIdy (interactive talks), Tiny (AI for schools), AutoResearch, colAIborate, open-source models ELSA and beeFormer.
- EU projects: PoliRuralPlus (Horizon Europe, rural policy with AI agents), FOCAL (forest and climate modelling), capTTict (technology transfer in 9 Danube countries).

## How to work with him

- PhD candidates (top priority): strong people for the group's research lines, ideally with company experience. Apply: https://kordikp.github.io/?type=phd#contact
- Research collaboration, joint proposals (Horizon Europe, national calls) and contract research in recommender systems and search, LLM agents and safety, ML for weather and climate, AI in education: https://kordikp.github.io/?type=research#contact
- Keynotes and talks: https://kordikp.github.io/?type=talk#contact
- Joining a project (Tiny, p-books, SlAIdy, AutoResearch, colAIborate, EduMatch): https://kordikp.github.io/?type=project#contact
- Helping AI dětem scale globally: https://kordikp.github.io/?type=aidetem#contact
- Bachelor's and master's theses: a limited number, for independent students who want to publish: https://kordikp.github.io/student-topics.html
- E-mail: kordik@gmail.com or kordikp@fit.cvut.cz

## Research themes

- Recommender systems & search: How to pick the right item for the right person: scalable autoencoders, cold start, honest evaluation and search. Most of it runs in production at Recombee.
- Language models, agents & AI safety: Text, explanations and AI agents: what language models know, how agents divide work in marketplaces, and how to keep chatbots safe, also for children.
- AI for science, health & climate: Machine learning on real measurements: weather nowcasting, climate and rural data, fluid simulations, medicine and forensic anthropology.
- Education, society & applied AI: AI for learning and for the people around it: education data, startups, skills and academia-industry matching.
- Neural networks & optimization: Neural networks, evolutionary algorithms and learned optimizers; from neuroevolution to transformers.
- Data mining, clustering & visualization: Finding structure in data: clustering (Chameleon), anomalies, time series and interactive visualization.
- Inductive modelling, meta-learning & AutoML: Letting algorithms build models: the GAME method, meta-learning templates, Predictor Factory and automated data mining.

## Eras

- 2002–2008, Inductive modelling: Student and Ph.D. years with prof. Miroslav Šnorek, starting from the GMDH method. The GAME method grows networks of heterogeneous neurons from data; ensembles of such models estimate their own credibility. First applications in medicine: sleep stages, atrial electrograms, fetal weight.
- 2009–2014, Meta-learning and data mining: At the new FIT CTU: meta-learning templates that combine models, the FAKE GAME open-source system, continuous optimization libraries, feature ranking, clustering and text mining. Most theses of this era build predictive models for real data.
- 2015–2019, From AutoML to recommender systems: Recombee is founded and the group turns to recommendation. In parallel: learning from relational data (Predictor Factory), multi-objective clustering (Chameleon 2) and predictive ensembles for transfer learning. The first doctoral students defend.
- 2020–2023, Deep learning in practice: Scalable shallow autoencoders (ELSA, VASP) and honest offline evaluation of recommenders; learned optimizers and physics-informed weather nowcasting with Meteopress; awards at NeurIPS, KDD and AAAI workshops.
- 2024–2026, Recommendation meets language models: Language and interaction signals merge (beeFormer, sparse embeddings), LLMs get explained and guarded (SHIELD, child-safety alignment, geo-grounded guardrails), AI agents start shopping on both sides of a marketplace, EU projects bring climate and rural data. RecSys 2025 comes to Prague; the p-book and RecSys Atlas open the field to newcomers.

## Milestones

- 2026 capTTict completed: Technology transfer and startup support across 9 Danube countries (2024–2026).
- 2026 Keynote at ISD 2026: “The Great Convergence: Recommendation, Search, and Conversation in Real-World AI Systems”.
- 2026 p-book and RecSys Atlas: A self-recommending living book (RecSys 2026 demo) and a map of 20 years of RecSys research.
- 2025 General Co-Chair, ACM RecSys 2025 in Prague: More than 1,000 attendees from around the world.
- 2024 Three EU projects start: PoliRuralPlus (Horizon Europe, CTU coordinates 20 partners), capTTict (Interreg Danube, CTU lead partner) and FOCAL (Horizon Europe).
- 2024 Co-founded edumatch.ai: Matching students with real-world opportunities in companies.
- 2024 ACM RecSys Steering Committee: Also Senior PC member of RecSys 2024.
- 2023 Best Paper Award, EvalRS @ KDD 2023: P. Kasalický, R. Alves, P. Kordík.
- 2022 1st place, Weather4cast 2022 (NeurIPS 2022): Core challenge won by the group (J. Pihrt, R. Raevskiy, P. Šimánek, M. Choma), in collaboration with Meteopress.
- 2021 Co-founded AI dětem: Teaching artificial intelligence to children at Czech schools.
- 2021 2nd place, Meta-Learning Challenge (AAAI 2021): T. Chobola, D. Vašata, P. Kordík.
- 2020 UniHack 2020: Co-organised an online hackathon of FIT CTU and prg.ai: in the first COVID spring, student teams and mentors looked for ways to help companies, the city, schools and healthcare.
- 2019 Co-founded prg.ai: Prague AI hub of the city, Charles University, the Czech Academy of Sciences and CTU.
- 2019 First doctoral students defended: Tomáš Řehořek (now leading Recombee) and Tomáš Bartoň.
- 2017 Associate Professor (doc.) in Informatics: Habilitation at FIT CTU.
- 2017 Vice-Dean for Industry Cooperation, FIT CTU (2017–2024): Ran the faculty's partnership programme with companies.
- 2017 Co-founded experts.ai: A platform connecting university experts with industry.
- 2015 Co-founded Recombee: Recommender systems as a service, now with customers worldwide; it works closely with the group at CTU.
- 2015 ECOOP 2015 in Prague: Organising committee of the European Conference on Object-Oriented Programming.
- 2011 Program committee, ACM KDD 2011
- 2010 Vice-Dean for Development, FIT CTU (2010–2016): Built up the young faculty; introduced master's courses Data Preprocessing, Data Mining Algorithms and Computational Intelligence Methods.
- 2009 Moved to the new Faculty of Information Technology: Founding years of FIT CTU; released the open-source FAKE GAME system for automated data mining.
- 2008 ICANN 2008 in Prague: Organising committee of the 18th International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks.
- 2007 Ph.D. on automated knowledge extraction: Dissertation on the GAME method (Group of Adaptive Models Evolution); organised the IWIM 2007 workshop in Prague.
- 2007 New course: Data Mining (FEE): Introduced the data mining course at CTU FEE together with Filip Železný.
- 2004 Joined the Department of Computer Science, CTU FEE: Started teaching and research in the computational intelligence group of prof. Miroslav Šnorek.
- 2003 Ing. in Computer Engineering, CTU FEE: Graduated from the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague.
